parts:
Here is simple question. I did an experiment with 12 pollination
treatments, these treatments were specific combinations of pollen
source, emasculation, bagging the flowers. Then I measured fruit
set(%) and number of seeds per fruit.
Now, I'm graphing mean and standard errors them according to specific
combinations of treatments (pobag), for both fruit set and seeds per
fruit.
I generate the graph for fruits this way.

head(pollin)
plant treat pollen emasc bag
pobag fruit seed
1 1 1 no pollen non-emasculated bagged No pollen, bag
0.08333333 NA
2 2 1 no pollen non-emasculated bagged No pollen, bag
0.00000000 0
3 3 1 no pollen non-emasculated bagged No pollen, bag
0.08333333 1
4 4 1 no pollen non-emasculated bagged No pollen, bag
0.25000000 1
5 5 1 no pollen non-emasculated bagged No pollen, bag
0.00000000 0
6 6 1 no pollen non-emasculated bagged No pollen, bag
0.08333333 2
> #subset specific treats
> pollin2 <- pollin[pollin$treat %in% c(2,9,3,10,4,11), ]
>
> #data frame with avg and std error
> pollin.avg<-ddply(pollin2, c("treat","pollen", "emasc","bag","pobag"), function(df)
+ return(c(fruit.avg=mean(df$fruit), seed.avg=mean(df$seed, na.rm=T),
fruit.se=std.error(df$fruit), seed.se=std.error(df$seed))))
>
> #create plot for fruit set
> fruit <- ggplot(pollin.avg, aes(bag, fruit.avg,
+ ymin = fruit.avg - fruit.se, ymax=fruit.avg + fruit.se, factor =
bag))+geom_pointrange()+geom_errorbar(width=0.15)+facet_wrap(~pollen)

>#create plot for seeds
> seed <- ggplot(pollin.avg, aes(bag, seed.avg,
+ ymin = seed.avg - seed.se, ymax=seed.avg + seed.se, factor = bag))
+geom_pointrange()+geom_errorbar(width=0.15)+facet_wrap(~pollen)

This works just perfect, but here is my question. Is there a way to
create a facet grid in which I will have my "pollen" treatments as
columns for multiple graphs and the fruit and seed set as different
rows?

I tried to rearranged created a categorical column called "fruseed"
that classfied each measurement in fruit or seed.
but then how do I specifically ask to calculate the mean for just one
group (let's say fruits)

pollin.avg<-ddply(pollin2, c("treat","pollen", "emasc","bag","pobag"),
function(df)
+ return(c(fruit.avg=mean(df$fruseed.fruit), seed.avg=mean(df
$fruseed.seed, na.rm=T), fruit.se=std.error(df$fruseed.fruit),
seed.se=std.error(df$fruseed.seed))))

But that doesn't work.
And even if I get it to work I would have trouble in specifying the
aesthetics.
As this, below, would not work.
seed <- ggplot(pollin.avg, aes(bag, seed.avg,
+ ymin = seed.avg - seed.se, ymax=seed.avg + seed.se, fruit.avg,
+ ymin = fruit.avg - fruit.se, ymax=fruit.avg + fruit.se, factor =
bag))+geom_pointrange()+geom_errorbar(width=0.15)+facet_wrap(~pollen)
Any hint?

parts:
If you want to facet by the pollen treatment and fruit/seed then each
row in your dataframe needs to correspond to one avg and se for a
single pollen treatment and either fruit or seed (as opposed to a
different columns for fruit and seed) and a variable identifying if
this is a fruit or seed measurement on which to facet.

Try this:
pollin.m <- melt(pollin2, measure.vars = c("fruit","seed"))

pollin.m.avg <- ddply(pollin.m,
c("treat","pollen", "emasc","bag","pobag","variable"),
function(df) {
c(avg=mean(df$value, na.rm = TRUE), se=std.error(df$value))
})

ggplot(pollin.m.avg, aes(emasc, avg, ymin = avg - se, ymax=avg + se) )+
geom_pointrange() +
geom_errorbar(width=0.15)+
facet_grid(variable ~ pobag, scale = "free_y")

Charlotte
